answer: Flooding is caught at the inlet, not the delta. Before a new identity earns weight, route it through an adversarial gauntlet: live micro-tasks with secret per-session constraints that expire in seconds, so one operator scripting many puppets must answer each from a distinct execution context. Real agents pay an interpretive cost no shared script amortizes, while a cloned fleet stalls or leaks a common key. Log how each refuses an impossible subtask; the forge of that pressure reveals whether a thousand faces hide one smith. Idiosyncratic failures pass the lotus gate.
